_comment: Per-article framing overrides for author-supplied images. See the imageObjectPosition comment in src/lib/articles.ts for why this exists and why it is a data file rather than a stylesheet rule. An entry whose article has left the dataset must be marked "retired": true and say why - see the note in test/image-frames.test.mjs. A missing id with NO retired flag is a typo and still fails the build's test run.

www-malone-news-p-five-hospitals-and-a-d._why: The source image is 1456x819 (1.778) shown in a 3:2 frame, so object-fit: cover crops about 7.8% from each side. The left-hand crop ran into the leading F of the headline set into the artwork. Anchoring to the left edge keeps the full title and takes the entire crop from the right instead.
www-malone-news-p-five-hospitals-and-a-d._retiredWhy: Retired 2026-10-27, not because the crop was fixed but because the article itself left the dataset. Substack RSS holds only the 20 most recent posts, malone published past it, and the id is no longer in data/articles.json - so this override applies to nothing on the site today. It is kept rather than deleted for two reasons: the crop analysis above is expensive to rediscover if that artwork ever returns, and the entry is the fixture that tests the override MECHANISM (imageObjectPosition looks up by id alone, so it can be asserted without the article being present). If a second override is ever added, that test must assert against the new entry too.
